summary: For thousands of years, legends have lived on the Moon. From China, the Jade Rabbit stirs elixirs of immortality. From Norse mythology, Hjúki and Bil fetch pails of water. From Inuit folklore, Igaluk chases his sun-sister Malina across the sky. Today, the Moon is getting new neighbors: NASA's Artemis astronauts! We created Moonkeepers, a cosy handdrawn RPG where you play as Pip the Star Pup, and throughout the mission, you help the ancient moon guardians sustain a world as educational as it is lovable. We teach players about life on the moon by having them manage a bustling lunar outpost, balancing competing demands like life support, radiation shielding, power, and food production, all while exploring the legends of ancient folklore. Our game is important because it makes the challenges of living on the Moon fun and accessible to everyone of all ages, without the heavy scientific barrier. Moonkeepers acts as a perfect entry way to learning about life on space, and its story is told in a way that engages the audience. Ultimately, the game encourages players to think critically, consider different trade-offs, and see themselves as people who could help shape the future of exploration.
details: The gameplay focuses on balancing different tasks in space in order to survive. Our game incorporates tasks such as maintaining water for food production, collecting solar power, and blocking dangerous radiation to make learning addictive. We used a blender animation for the opening scene using three.js (javascript), where they can flip through a book to learn about the game and its characters, and RBG maker to create the actual game settings. All the art and characters are hand drawn by our team members on Ibis Paintx and Autodesk sketchbook. Our project uniquely integrates cultural folklore and scientific data to create a story that truly resonates with the audience, and have them develop connections to each character they help while achieving their goal. Moonkeepers was designed to bring awareness to the challenges astronauts face while living in extreme conditions, and create accessibility for kids and students of any age to easily understand and learn about them. We considered multiple factors, including how to best hook them in and engage with the player, how to make the game fun while still being as scientifically correct as possible, and how to integrate multiple different features into one game.
